title: Fractions
description: Class 6 IMO — Fractions: types, equivalent fractions and simplest form, comparison, and addition, subtraction, multiplication and division of fractions with word problems.

topics.title: Types, Equivalent Fractions & Simplest Form
topics.concept:
A proper fraction has numerator < denominator, an improper fraction has numerator ≥ denominator, and a mixed fraction is a whole number with a fraction.

Equivalent fractions show the same value (½ = 2/4). The simplest form is found by dividing the numerator and denominator by their HCF: 8/12 = 2/3.
recap: Simplest form: divide top and bottom by their HCF.

quiz.q: Which of these is an improper fraction?
quiz.explanation: In 5/2 the numerator is larger than the denominator.

topics.title: Comparison, Addition & Subtraction
topics.concept:
To compare or add/subtract unlike fractions, change them to the same denominator (the LCM) first, then work with the numerators.

So ⅓ + ¼ = 4/12 + 3/12 = 7/12, and ⅚ − ½ = 5/6 − 3/6 = ⅓.
recap: Use a common denominator (the LCM) for unlike fractions.
Then add or subtract the numerators.

topics.title: Multiplication, Division & Word Problems
topics.concept:
The "Keep-Change-Flip" Rule

Dividing fractions is easy with this trick:

Keep the first fraction

Change ÷ to ×

Flip the second fraction (reciprocal)

Rule: (a)/(b) ÷ (c)/(d) = (a)/(b) × (d)/(c) = (a × d)/(b × c)

Examples:

  • ⅔ ÷ ⅘ = ⅔ × 5/4 = 10/12 = (5)/(6)
  • ⅚ ÷ ⅓ = ⅚ × 3/1 = 15/6 = 5/2 = 2½

Dividing Mixed Numbers:

  1. Convert mixed numbers to improper fractions
  2. Use Keep-Change-Flip
  3. Simplify
KEEP-CHANGE-FLIP VISUAL:

    2   ÷   4    =    2   ×   5
    3       5         3       4
    
    KEEP    CHANGE    FLIP
    2/3      ×        5/4
    
    Multiply: 2×5=10, 3×4=12, 10/12 = 5/6


VISUAL REPRESENTATION: ½ ÷ ¼

    "How many ¼ are in ½?"
    
    ½ of a whole:    
    ┌─────────────────┐
    │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
    └─────────────────┘
    
    ¼ of a whole:     
    ┌─────────┐
    │░░░░░░░░░│
    └─────────┘
    
    Count how many ¼ fit into ½:
    
    ┌─────────┬─────────┐
    │░░░░░░░░░│░░░░░░░░░│
    └─────────┴─────────┘
        ¼        ¼
    
    Answer: 2 (½ ÷ ¼ = 2)


DIVIDING MIXED NUMBERS:

    2⅓ ÷ 1½ = ?
    
    Step 1: Convert to improper fractions
    2⅓ = 7/3, 1½ = 3/2
    
    Step 2: Keep-Change-Flip
    7/3 ÷ 3/2 = 7/3 × 2/3
    
    Step 3: Multiply
    7×2=14, 3×3=9, 14/9 = 1⁵⁄₉
recap: Divide: multiply by the reciprocal of the second fraction.
